summary: Edeltraud Harzer worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Charles University, the University of Washington (PhD), and under traditional teachers Shrinarayan Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held posts at Washington, Puget Sound, Stanford, Indiana, and UT Austin (emeritus 1998).

Linguist Edgar Howard Sturtevant studied at Illinois College (1893–1895) and Indiana University Bloomington (~1895–1898). He taught Murray Barnson Emeneau and held academic posts at Columbia University (~1907–1920) and Yale University (~1927–1943).

Edgar Polomé worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Université catholique de Louvain (~1938–1949) and was a professor, later professor emeritus, at the University of Texas at Austin (~1961–1993).
Edgar Thurston, who worked in history and archaeology, studied at Eton College and King's College London. He served as Superintendent of the Government Museum, Chennai, from around 1885 to 1908.

Edith Wyschogrod worked in philosophy and religious studies. She earned a B.A. from Hunter College (~1947–1951) and a Ph.D. from Columbia University (-1970), later serving as J. Newton Rayzor Professor at Rice University (1992–2002).
Working in religious studies and sinology, Edmond Yee held faculty posts at Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union, both around 1988.

Edmund Hardy worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Mainz, Berlin, Heidelberg (PhD under Kuno Fischer), and Freiburg. He held professorships at Freiburg (1885–1893), Fribourg (1894–1898), and Würzburg (~1893–1904).

Philosopher Edmund Husserl studied under Wilhelm Wundt at Leipzig, Berlin, Vienna, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1887–1901), Göttingen (1901–1916), and Freiburg (1916–1928), teaching Tanabe, Yamauchi, and Heidegger.

Edmund Leach studied at Clare College, Cambridge (BA) and the London School of Economics (PhD). He taught at the LSE (~1947–1953) and the University of Cambridge (1953–1978), where he also served as Provost of King's College (1966–1979).
Indologist Edmund Nathaniel Snyder graduated as valedictorian from Harvard University in 1886. He also pursued studies under teachers Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

Edo Shonin works in religious and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2015, he held posts as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

Linguist Eduard Böhmer studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1847–1851). He later held academic posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1859–1872) and the University of Strasbourg (~1872–1879).

Sinologist Eduard Erkes studied at the University of Leipzig (~1908–1913) under doctoral supervisor August Conrady, whom he later succeeded. He held posts at the University of Leipzig (~1917–1958) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1948–1950).

Eduard Hermann worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Leipzig, Freiburg, and Jena (PhD under Berthold Delbrück). He held posts at Kiel (1913), Frankfurt (1914), and the University of Göttingen (Professor, 1917–1937).

Eduard Müller was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed an inaugural dissertation at the University of Leipzig (~1872–1874) and later served as a professor at the University of Bern (~1886–1908).

Indologist and philosopher Eduard Röer studied at Königsberg and Jena under J.F. Herbart, and later under Franz Bopp. He held a postdoctorate at Berlin (1833), worked for the East India Company, and held multiple posts at The Asiatic Society.

Eduard Sachau studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Halle-Wittenberg under Brockhaus, Fleischer, and Nöldeke. Working in Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies, he was professor at Vienna (1869) and Berlin (from 1876), also directing the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1887).
Linguist and Indologist Eduard Schwyzer held academic appointments at the University of Zurich (~1912–1927), the University of Bonn (~1927–1932), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932–1943).

Linguist Eduard Sievers studied at Leipzig, Humboldt University, and Berlin under Curtius, Leskien, and Zarncke. He served as professor at Jena (1871–1883), Tübingen (1883–1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887–1892), and held the German Philology chair at Leipzig (1892–1922).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under supervisors Yakupitiyage Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.
